the_read: Three pre-launch and just-launched titles are doing more attention per dollar than the rest of the universe combined this week. Forza Horizon 6 at 57K live Twitch viewers three days pre-launch with 3.3M wishlists is the rare cross-platform AAA where Game Pass cannibalisation is the only binding question. the_read_by_cadence.weekly: The weekly filter cuts the daily noise: the universe right now is rich with first-of-publisher and pivot bets. Pocketpair Publishing's Windrose ($46M revenue, 1.95M owners in 30 days) is the proof-of-concept for a structural play — a small-studio publishing line capturing the niche nobody has institutionalised. Shiro Games' Farever pivots a grand-strategy studio into action-RPG (contested loop, engaged cohort). Mega Crit shipping StS 2 alone is the cleanest "no publisher needed" case on file. the_read_by_cadence.monthly: The month's structural read is that wishlist counts above 3M are no longer rare. Forza Horizon 6, Subnautica 2, GTA VI, Hogwarts Legacy at its pre-launch peak — all four crossed the threshold. The 3M-wishlist bar used to be once-a-year; it's now four times per year and counting. That changes pre-launch marketing economics: wishlist accumulation as a one-time playable-demo-fed campaign is being replaced by multi-year drip-cohort accumulation. Studios who can't run that long campaign are at a structural disadvantage. The corollary: the highest-EV pre-launch indicator is no longer wishlist count, it's wishlist persistence — does the count hold through delay announcements, sequel reveals, content gaps. That's the new diagnostic.

the_read: Forza Horizon 6 is launching with 3.33M wishlists — that's a top-3 wishlist conversion event of the era, behind only Hogwarts Legacy and BG3.
57,000 concurrent Twitch viewers three days before launch with 96 streams running is pre-launch broadcast saturation. Xbox marketing got their money's worth from the streamer outreach.

Playground Games + Xbox Game Studios + 224K followers means the launch number is bounded only by Steam infrastructure. The interesting commercial question is the long-tail attach rate to Game Pass — every Game Pass subscriber who plays this is one less Steam purchase.
thesis.against_consensus: Consensus treats this as a guaranteed phenom-tier launch. Look closer: the post-Forza-5 retention curve was flatter than the franchise's prior median, and the audience that bounced on FH5 hasn't been re-recruited yet. Phenom on day-one peak, but the cohort settle is the real question.
thesis.comparable: Forza Horizon 5 at launch ran 71K peak CCU on Steam at a moment with lower wishlist counts. FH6's 3.3M wishlists are roughly 1.6× higher — projects to 110-130K Steam peak CCU if conversion holds, or 70-80K if Game Pass cannibalises Steam more heavily than FH5.
thesis.what_would_change_my_mind: A weekend-1 Steam peak below 60K would signal Game Pass cannibalisation is steeper than projected and the franchise plateau is real.
risks: Game Pass overlap caps Steam-side commercial upside.
Franchise plateau risk from FH5 retention shape.
thesis.pull_quote: Top-3 wishlist conversion of the era. Launch number is bounded only by infrastructure.

the_read: Slay the Spire 2 is the highest-revenue EA launch on file: $129M booked in 70 days. Mega Crit shipped without a publisher and kept every dollar.

63% positive on 158K reviews is conspicuously mixed for the genre-defining studio. Cohort split is between original-StS purists complaining about deviations and new-cohort players. The next two patches resolve it either direction.
Steam owners cleared 6.8M units in 70 days at $25 SRP. This is what happens when the original's audience converts on a sequel with zero marketing budget.
thesis.against_consensus: Industry press hand-wringing about mixed reviews is misreading the signal. 6.8M units in 10 weeks with 158K reviews is the kind of engagement curve publishers spend a hundred million to manufacture. Reviews are mixed because lots of people are playing, not because the product is failing.
thesis.comparable: Original Slay the Spire's EA run captured ~250K reviews over 18 months. StS 2 hit 158K in 10 weeks — roughly 12× the review velocity. Projects to a long-tail outcome comparable to the original's ~$200M lifetime, with upside if Mega Crit nails the patch cadence.
thesis.what_would_change_my_mind: Two more weeks of declining concurrent + reviews going net-negative. Currently the velocity says the cohort is engaged, not disengaged.
risks: Sequel-purity backlash is the operational risk; patch cadence is the lever.
Roguelike-deckbuilder cluster is now saturated with imitators.
thesis.pull_quote: $129M booked in 70 days with no publisher. Mixed reviews are engagement, not failure.

the_read: Crimson Desert is at week 8 post-launch with $30M+ revenue tracking and signal compression. The Korean MMO-team-makes-action-game pivot delivered an actual cohort.
Pearl Abyss took 9 years to ship this from announcement. The launch curve is the patient-capital benchmark — most studios couldn't sustain that runway.
73% positive on 18K reviews with persistent Twitch presence post-launch is the second-wave-eligible shape. The interesting commercial question is the China-region rollout cadence.
thesis.against_consensus: Consensus over-discounted Crimson Desert because of the 9-year dev cycle. The launch performance shows that long-runway development is still viable for studios with prior cash buffer. The structural lesson is harder to extract than the SKU outcome.
thesis.comparable: Black Desert at week 8 post-launch (the predecessor): similar review velocity, slightly higher CCU floor. Crimson Desert is tracking ~80% of BDO's curve at the same window — predictable, not surprising.
thesis.what_would_change_my_mind: A 30-day decline in Korean-region CCU. Pearl Abyss's commercial model is more dependent on Asia rollout than Western markets.
risks: 9-year dev cycle was operationally expensive — payback period is the analyst question.
thesis.pull_quote: The patient-capital benchmark. Most studios couldn't sustain a 9-year runway.

the_read: PRAGMATA delivered Capcom's cleanest review-velocity launch since Resident Evil 4 Remake — 41,901 reviews at 97% positive in 30 days. The 8-year dev cycle paid off.

$42.5M revenue with 1.15M owners on a $40 SKU in a month puts this in the Hit band on day-1 numbers. Capcom's marketing efficiency was unusually high here — wishlist conversion was over 40%, ~2× the AAA cluster median.
236 IGDB hypes is the highest of any launched product in this universe. The cohort came in hot and stayed.
thesis.against_consensus: Consensus underweighted Pragmata's commercial upside because of the long delays. The launch data shows the delays were the right call — patience built a wider, more sentiment-aligned cohort than a 2022 launch would have captured.
thesis.comparable: Resident Evil 4 Remake at week 4 post-launch: 80K reviews at 96% positive, $200M revenue, 4.2M owners. Pragmata is at roughly half-scale on every metric, which is the right relative position for a new-IP Capcom product vs. franchise tentpole.
thesis.what_would_change_my_mind: A 30-day Twitch decline past 60% would suggest the product is short-loop and won't sustain. Currently the curve looks like a long-tail-eligible single-player narrative.
risks: Single-player narrative cohort has limited replay incentive.
Capcom's DLC roadmap is unclear — that's the long-tail lever.
thesis.pull_quote: Capcom's cleanest review-velocity launch since RE4 Remake. The 8-year dev cycle paid off.

the_read: Windrose has booked $46.6M revenue in 30 days at 87% positive — Pocketpair Publishing's first non-Palworld bet is the read here.
1.95M owners on a $25 SKU in one month is publisher-validation territory. Pocketpair has turned its post-Palworld cash pile into a publishing line and Windrose is the proof of concept.
Kraken Express the developer is unknown outside of this. The interesting commercial question is whether Pocketpair's publishing apparatus is the structural value or just lucky once.
thesis.against_consensus: Consensus reads Windrose as a Palworld-style co-op survival outlier. The harder question is what Pocketpair Publishing as a structural entity becomes — they are positioning to capture the 'small studio with proven loop, no publisher overhead' niche nobody has institutionalised yet.
thesis.comparable: Palworld at the equivalent week-4 post-launch sat at ~700K reviews and 18M owners. Windrose is at 41K reviews / 1.95M owners — roughly 1/10 the magnitude, which puts it in the Cult band, not Phenom. The interesting bet is the publishing pipeline behind it.
thesis.what_would_change_my_mind: If Pocketpair's next publishing pick lands flat, the structural thesis breaks and Windrose becomes a one-shot.
risks: Unknown dev studio — track record uncertain post-Pocketpair handover.
